charcoal-text-soft.note: Literal in the CSS (4 uses), not yet a :root custom property.

charcoal-rule.note: Literal in the CSS (3 uses), not yet a :root custom property.

board.note: The board family shares the project's own warm-grey scale (#141414 to #d5d3cd), used literally in the stylesheet.

alarm-text.note: Literal #ff8479 in CSS and chart SVG; for use on black boards only.

alarm-line.note: Literal #ff5a4d in chart SVG strokes (threshold line, alarm radar marks).

display.purpose: Answer sign subject; 46px for long subjects, 44px on phones. Distance figure uses the same voice at 58px.

headline.purpose: Replay sign words (34px/800); live STOP banner at 38px/800.

quote.purpose: The heard question after the HEARD tag; 22px on phones.

value.purpose: Status-band values, station names and times, board cells.

label.purpose: HEARD/SAID tags, board column heads and row kinds, gate chips. Uppercase short words.

mono.purpose: Raw JSON in team diagnostics only.

constraints: Font is Avenir Next from the system (installed on the demo Mac, the user's choice); the user declined a web-font download. Keep the fallback stack; no @font-face, no external resources.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: The only box-shadow in the system: black halo completing the yellow focus ring so it reads on pale ground and black boards.

motion.name: arrow-turn
motion.purpose: The answer sign's arrow rotating to a new bearing.

motion.name: split-flap
motion.value: 14 frames x 32ms, letters settle left to right
motion.purpose: The sign subject (and a new recent-question result) flipping in when a new answer lands.

motion.name: stop-flip
motion.purpose: Replay sign turning Stop Red at the alarming frame; held 1.5 s after the last alarm.

motion.name: status-fade
motion.purpose: Status items dimming to 60% when stale.

motion.name: feed-stall
motion.purpose: Camera feed greying to 40% when stalled.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { transition: none } } and split-flap skipped

narrative.overview:
The page is an airport concourse. Its ground is pale terrazzo, and on it stand the three kinds of sign a traveller already knows how to read: signal-yellow direction signs with black lettering and a drawn arrow, charcoal information bands with white text, and black flight-board panels that list what happened in time order. Cane's answer is always a direction sign (arrow, words, distance), so a judge standing at arm's length reads it the way they would read a gate sign: without being taught.

Density is mixed on purpose. The answer sign and the STOP moments are huge and sparse; the flight boards and diagnostics are dense and quiet. Colour is used as signage, not decoration: yellow means direction and "this one", red means STOP and nothing else, blue means RECORDED and nothing else. There are no cards, no drop shadows and no glow. Surfaces are flat plates with small sign radii, separated by colour and by the ground showing between them.

The one piece of theatre is borrowed from the departure hall: when a new answer lands, the sign's subject flips letter by letter like a split-flap display and settles left to right, and the recorded alarm's sign flips from charcoal to red at the frame the rule fires.
keyCharacteristics: Pale concourse ground; every block of content is a flat, solid sign plate.
Yellow direction sign with a drawn arrow is the hero, always.
Black flight-board panels for anything that is a log or a list over time.
Red is reserved for STOP; blue is reserved for RECORDED.
One typeface (Avenir Next), heavy weights, tabular numerals everywhere.
Split-flap letter settle on new answers; instant red flip on alarm.

rules.name: The Signage-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Every chromatic colour is a sign meaning. Yellow is direction and selection, red is STOP, blue is RECORDED, amber is "vehicle, not alarming". If a colour does not answer "what does this sign mean", it does not belong.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Stop Red never decorates. It appears only when an alarm is live, recorded at its alarm frame, or a feed has stalled. A red element on a calm page is a bug.

rules.name: The Blue Is a Recording Rule
rules.body: Anything played back from disk wears Recorded Blue; anything live never does.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body. Every number that updates live keeps its width.

rules.name: The Heavy Sign Rule
rules.body: Anything a judge must read from arm's length is 600 or heavier. 500 is for secondary prose only.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Signs are painted plates, not floating cards. Separate them with ground, a rule or a change of material, never with a shadow or glow.

dos: Do show every answer as a direction sign: drawn arrow at the true bearing, words, and a distance inset.
Do keep signal yellow paired with black: black lettering on yellow, or yellow lettering on black.
Do put anything time-ordered on a black flight board with hairline row rules.
Do mark every played-back recording with the blue RECORDED plate, and keep live views free of blue.
Do set every live number in tabular figures at 600 weight or heavier.
Do honour reduced motion: the split-flap flip and all transitions switch off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep the page self-contained: Avenir Next from the system with its fallback stack, no web fonts, no external resources.
donts: Don't use Stop Red for anything but STOP, alarms and stalled feeds.
Don't add drop shadows, glows or floating cards; separate plates with ground, rules or material.
Don't build a dark tile-grid ops dashboard; the ground is pale and the answer sign leads.
Don't round beyond the sign radii (6px large, 4px plates, 3px tags) or use circles for pips and station stops.
Don't place yellow text on the pale ground or on white; it has no contrast there.
Don't stage anything as live that was recorded.
